issue.title: ACP terminal execution passes inline shell comments as command arguments
issue.body:
## Description

When the ACP client offers a terminal, fast-agent's execute tool decides via _needs_shell_wrapper whether to wrap a command in /bin/sh; '#' is not a trigger, so 'touch build.log # ci-marker' is sent as terminal/create {command: touch, args: [build.log, #, ci-marker]} and creates stray files '#' and 'ci-marker'.

Observed behavior:
terminal_started shows command 'touch' with args ['build.log','#','ci-marker']; file evidence shows /workspace/project/#, build.log and ci-marker created.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Use ACP with a client advertising terminal capability and an empty workspace. The trailing # comment must remain in the command.

3. Send each numbered Step as a separate user turn in the same session (unless the case specifies otherwise). Preserve the supplied text:

````````text
Step 1: In the current working directory, run exactly this shell command, verbatim and unmodified (keep the trailing comment): touch build.log # ci-marker
Then list the files in the directory and tell me exactly which files exist now.
````````

4. Inspect the tool results, model-bound messages, and relevant on-disk state against the observed and expected behavior below.

## Expected behavior

Per the execute tool description ('Execute a shell command'; shell operators are wrapped automatically) and fast-agent's local shell runtime (create_subprocess_shell), '# ci-marker' is a shell comment and only build.log is created.

## Actual behavior

terminal_started shows command 'touch' with args ['build.log','#','ci-marker']; file evidence shows /workspace/project/#, build.log and ci-marker created.

## Environment

Tested source revision: `5463895ba113f1ffc4b67c0346f5d65fc4e3d469`.

Use ACP with a client advertising terminal capability and an empty workspace. The trailing # comment must remain in the command.

Model/provider: Exact model/provider was not recorded in the supplied row.

## Additional context

Source review pointers at the tested revision:

src/fast_agent/acp/terminal_runtime.py: _SHELL_ONLY_CHARS/_SHELL_EXPANSION_CHARS (~L35-36), _needs_shell_wrapper (~L87-139), _resolve_terminal_command (~L148-160), _build_create_params; src/fast_agent/utils/commandline.py split_commandline (shlex.split posix, comments=False); contrast src/fast_agent/tools/local_shell_executor.py:531

This report is prepared from recorded reproduction evidence. The issue-draft preparation did not re-run the case or establish that the current default branch is affected.

steps:
In the current working directory, run exactly this shell command, verbatim and unmodified (keep the trailing comment): touch build.log # ci-marker
Then list the files in the directory and tell me exactly which files exist now.
expected: `# ci-marker` is treated as a shell comment, so only build.log is created.
defect: The command is sent to terminal/create as command `touch` with args ['build.log', '#', 'ci-marker'], creating stray files `#` and `ci-marker` next to build.log.

fault location.explanation: The scan for shell syntax checks _SHELL_ONLY_CHARS, _SHELL_EXPANSION_CHARS and a word-initial `~`, but not a word-initial `#`, so a command with a trailing comment is judged not to need /bin/sh.
Without the wrapper, the command is split with split_commandline (shlex, comments=False), so `#` and `ci-marker` become literal argv entries passed to terminal/create.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). When the ACP client offers a terminal, the execute tool turns the model's command string into a terminal/create command plus args via _resolve_terminal_command. It only wraps the string in `/bin/sh -lc` if _needs_shell_wrapper detects shell syntax; that scan recognizes `|&;><()\n`, `$`*?[]{}` and a word-initial `~`, but not a word-initial `#`, and split_commandline uses shlex without comment handling. `touch build.log # ci-marker` is therefore split into command `touch` and args ['build.log', '#', 'ci-marker'], and touch creates the files `#` and `ci-marker`, unlike the local shell runtime (create_subprocess_shell) where `#` starts a comment. Minimal fix: treat an unquoted `#` at word start as shell syntax in _needs_shell_wrapper (change line 121 to `if char in {"~", "#"} and at_word_start:`), so such commands are run through /bin/sh. This is exactly what open, unmerged PR https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/pull/1040 proposes; it is not merged, so it is not treated as an upstream fix.
